title: Benchmarking and Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models

problem.claim: Integrating large language models with external content creates vulnerability to indirect prompt injection attacks, in which malicious instructions embedded in that content can manipulate model outputs.

gap.claim: Indirect prompt injection attacks are described as a critical yet under-explored issue lacking a benchmark for assessing vulnerability risk.

contributions.claim: The work introduces BIPIA, a benchmark for assessing vulnerability to indirect prompt injection attacks.
The work proposes boundary awareness and explicit reminder defense mechanisms for black-box and white-box settings.

The work analyzes factors associated with attack success, including difficulty distinguishing informational context from actionable instructions and avoiding execution of instructions in external content.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe BIPIA as the first benchmark for indirect prompt injection attacks and the two defense mechanisms as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Using BIPIA, the authors report that evaluated existing LLMs were universally vulnerable.
The authors report that their black-box defense provides substantial mitigation.
The authors report that their white-box defense reduces attack success rates to near-zero levels while preserving LLM output quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM integration with external content enables applications but introduces indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities.
Malicious instructions in external content can manipulate outputs and cause deviations from user expectations.
The authors introduce BIPIA to assess the risk of indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities.
The authors report universal vulnerability among evaluated LLMs and identify two contributing factors.
The authors propose two defenses and report mitigation, near-zero attack success for the white-box defense, and preserved output quality.

source_observation.claim: The authors attribute attack success partly to LLMs' inability to distinguish informational context from actionable instructions.

interpretation.claim: Systems that combine external content with model instructions need an explicit boundary between information and executable directives.

application.claim: Design external-content pipelines to mark content boundaries and separately represent untrusted content and actionable instructions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether boundary marking is sufficient across models, tasks, or attack types.

source_observation.claim: The authors report that explicit reminders and boundary awareness mitigated attacks while preserving output quality in their experiments.

interpretation.claim: Lightweight instruction-hygiene mechanisms may reduce indirect prompt injection risk without necessarily degrading responses.

application.claim: Evaluate reminder- and boundary-based safeguards as candidate controls for LLM applications that process untrusted external content.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the evaluated tasks, threat coverage, or conditions under which output quality was preserved.

unknowns: Benchmark composition, attack categories, and evaluation metrics are unspecified.
The evaluated LLMs, experimental settings, baselines, and comparison details are unspecified.
The mechanisms and implementation requirements of the black-box and white-box defenses are unspecified.
